QF.id: Securities Types Features and Asset Allocation Concepts_5

question.text: When a company chooses not to distribute its profits as dividends and instead keeps them within the company, these undistributed profits are called:

explanation.text: The Logic: The share of profits not distributed to shareholders is known as retained profits. These become part of the company's reserve funds. Reserves belong to the shareholders though they remain with the company until distributed as dividends. They enhance the net worth of the company and the value of equity shares. The Trap: Paid-up capital (option B) is the amount actually paid by shareholders for their shares. Authorized capital (option C) is the maximum capital a company can issue. Debenture redemption fund (option D) is a specific reserve for repaying debentures. Note: Retained profits and reserves are defined in the NISM XII workbook (page 40) as undistributed profits that belong to shareholders and enhance equity-share value.
